content: 1. Ethinylestradiol levels can be reduced by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 3. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 4. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 5. Pioglitazone decreases ethinylestradiol levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Primidone reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 8. Concomitant use of hormonal contraceptives with certain drugs may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, and menorrhagia. Close monitoring is required. 9. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Rabeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ranolazine levels or effects are increased by ethinylestradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Rasagiline levels or effects are increased by ethinylestradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Females should use effective nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 16. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 18. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 19. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 21. Romidepsin decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through receptor binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Ropinirole levels are increased by ethinylestradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Rosuvastatin increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 25. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rufinamide is a weak CYP3A4 inducer and may decrease the exposure of CYP3A4 substrates. 26. Ruxolitinib levels are increased by ethinylestradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Ferrous fumarate absorption is decreased by sodium bicarbonate, sodium citrate/citric acid, and other agents that increase gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents to avoid chelation. 28. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 29. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of somapacitan, somatrogon, and somatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring higher GH doses. 30. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 31. Stiripentol affects the metabolism of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by acting as both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for increased or decreased effects, and adjust dosages as needed. 32. Sugammadex decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by receptor binding competition. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients must use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for 7 days after administration. 33. Sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, and sulfisoxazole decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Tacrolimus levels are increased by ethinylestradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism.
